\begin{lemma}[Simulation of an Embedded Phase]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_phase}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_phase}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM.splitSafe, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_mapState_of_agreeOn, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, $S,H$ types, and $x$ a Boolean input word. Let a source
machine with $k$ work tapes and a host machine with $l$ work tapes be given, along with
a tape embedding $\iota:\text{Fin}(k)\hookrightarrow\text{Fin}(l)$, a state embedding
$e:S\hookrightarrow H$, an anchor state $a\in H$, and a predicate $P$ on source states.
Suppose no state in the image of $e$ is $a$, and whenever $P(q)$ holds, the host
transition at $e(q)$ agrees, for every input symbol and work-tape reading, with the
embedded source transition followed by the state map $e$. For background tape contents
and head positions, source configurations $c,d$, and $t\in\mathbb{N}$, suppose every
source state reached at a time $j<t$ satisfies $P$, and the source run from $c$ reaches
$d$ at time $t$. Then the host run from the embedded, state-mapped configuration of $c$
reaches the corresponding embedded, state-mapped configuration of $d$ at time $t$, and
none of its configurations at times $0$ through $t$ has state $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Simulation of an embedded call phase]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_call_phase}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_call_phase}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.mapState_apply, Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_phase, Turing.FinTM.splitSafe, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{6}
Let $S,H$ be state types, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let a source machine with
$k$ work tapes and a host machine with $l$ work tapes both use the Boolean alphabet. Let
$\iota$ inject the source tape indices into the host tape indices, and let $e:S\to H$ be
an injective state map. Choose host states $e_0$ and $a_0$ with $e_0\ne a_0$, and assume
$e(q)\ne a_0$ for every source state $q$. Let $q_e,q_x$ be source states. Suppose the
host transition at $e_0$, for every input and work-tape reading, is the source
transition from $q_e$ with its state renamed by $e$; and at each state $e(q)$ with $q\ne
q_x$, the host transition agrees in the same way with the source transition from $q$.
For any host tape contents and head positions, any prefix output list, source
configurations $c,d$ with $c$ in state $q_e$, and any $t>0$, if the source run avoids
$q_x$ at every time strictly between $0$ and $t$ and reaches $d$ at time $t$, then the
host run from the configuration formed by embedding $c$ into the host tapes, preserving
the other host tapes and prefixing the output by the given list, with state set to
$e_0$, reaches the correspondingly embedded configuration from $d$ with state renamed by
$e$ at time $t$. The host run has no configuration in state $a_0$ at any time from $0$
through $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Framed configuration embedding]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_frame}
\label{Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_pos, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_tape, Turing.embedEmitTM_frame}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $x$ be a finite Boolean
input word, choose $q\in S$, and let $\iota$ inject the $k$ source tape indices into the
$l$ host tape indices. Let $e:S\to H$ be a map, let
$T_j:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$ and $h_j\in\mathbb{Z}$ specify ambient
contents and head positions for each host tape $j$, and let $c$ and $d$ be
configurations on $x$ with $k$ and $l$ work tapes and state sets $S$ and $H$,
respectively. Suppose the optional state of $c$, mapped by $e$, equals the optional
state of $d$; their input-head positions and outputs agree; and for each source tape
$i$, its contents and head position in $c$ equal those of host tape $\iota(i)$ in $d$.
Suppose also that for every host tape $j$ outside the image of $\iota$, $T_j$ and $h_j$
equal its contents and head position in $d$. Then embedding $c$ into the host tapes
using these ambient contents and head positions, with empty output prefix, and mapping
its state by $e$ gives exactly $d$.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Turing.FinTM.splitSolveWithTM_computes}
\label{Turing.FinTM.splitSolveWithTM_computes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.callEntry, Turing.FinTM.callExit, Turing.FinTM.callTM, Turing.FinTM.callTM_k_pos, Turing.FinTM.callTM_run, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.emitterP2BodyTM, Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_body_round, Turing.FinTM.emitterP2_body_start, Turing.FinTM.emitterSplitAccept, Turing.FinTM.emitterSplit_loop_bound, Turing.FinTM.emitterSplit_result, Turing.FinTM.emitter_width_budget, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM, Turing.FinTM.lengthBitsTM_computes, Turing.FinTM.loopHostTM_finds, Turing.FinTM.splitSolveWithTM, Turing.FinTM.splitStep, Turing.FinTM.splitStep_inv, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.solveSplitWith, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean
alphabet, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be monotone. Suppose that on every Boolean
word $s$, $E$ halts within $T(|s|)$ steps and outputs the binary expansion of $f(|s|)$.
Then the machine built from $E$ computes, on every Boolean word $w$, the pairing of the
prefix of length $i$ and the remaining suffix when $i$ is the least number satisfying
$i+f(i)=|w|$; if no such $i$ exists, it outputs the empty word. Its running time on
inputs of length $n$ is at most $20(591+26k)(n+1)(T(n+1)+n+2)$, where $k$ is the number
of work tapes of $E$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Unary token transducer]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.unaryTokenTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.unaryTokenTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
Define a Boolean Turing machine with no work tapes and six control states. Starting at
the left end of its input, it outputs each input bit; it outputs one additional $0$ at
the right end, followed by one $1$, then halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Running time of unary token encoding]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.unaryTokenTM_computes}
\label{Turing.FinTM.unaryTokenTM_computes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.unaryTokenTM, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.unaryTokenSplit}
The specified finite Turing machine computes, on every Boolean string $x$, the encoding
of the token and remainder obtained by splitting off the maximal leading block of true
bits together with its terminating false bit, or the entire string if there is no false
bit. Its running time on an input of length $n$ is $3(n+1)$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Machine that appends a bit]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.appendBitTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.appendBitTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
For each bit $b$, define a finite Turing machine with no work tapes, a single state, and
that state as its initial state. When it reads a symbol, it moves the input head one
step to the right, outputs the symbol, and remains in the state; when it reads a blank,
it outputs $b$ and halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Appending a bit to a Boolean word]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.appendBitTM_computes}
\label{Turing.FinTM.appendBitTM_computes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.appendBitTM}
For every bit $b \in \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and every finite Boolean word
$x$, there exists a space usage $s \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the machine that appends
$b$ halts after exactly $|x|+1$ steps on input $x$, has output $x$ followed by $b$, and
uses exactly $s$ work-tape cells.
\end{theorem}
